page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 CPU architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server integrates a single NVIDIA Tesla P4 graphics processor equipped with 8 GB of video RAM (VRAM) to handle hardware-accelerated workloads.

The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps and relies entirely on remote cloud storage, as no local storage is bundled with the host hardware. By offloading parallel computing tasks to the discrete NVIDIA P4 GPU, this instance delivers graphics and inference acceleration relative to its moderate general-compute footprint. The lack of ephemeral local storage necessitates reliance on attached block volumes, introducing network dependency for disk-intensive operations.

From a resource density perspective, combining a lower-power inference GPU with moderate CPU and memory capacity makes this instance a cost-efficient option for lightweight GPU workloads. Suitable workload fits include AI and machine learning model inference, video transcoding, real-time image processing, and remote graphics rendering.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server built on x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor. It comes equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 16.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core), and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features a single discrete NVIDIA Tesla P4 GPU offering 8 GB of VRAM, designed for GPU-bound computing tasks. The server lacks local ephemeral disk storage, requiring external block storage attachment for data retention and disk operations. This configuration delivers a cost-efficient resource profile by pairing modest general-compute specifications with dedicated graphics acceleration. The balance of 4 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM, and an NVIDIA P4 GPU makes the server well suited for low-density machine learning inference, video streaming and transcoding, real-time image processing, and remote graphics rendering tasks.
